thread:
Maya: Ok team — we need to lock down the compliance roadmap for the next quarter. SOC2 work, audit log retention, and the KMS/HSM customer asks are all competing for the same eng capacity. Can we agree on priorities and launch criteria?

Daniel: Quick context — a couple of enterprise prospects asked for FIPS-backed HSM integration and 7-year audit log retention. We promised to present a realistic timeline in the next exec review.

Sara: From infra side: SOC2 controls (logging + monitoring gaps) are highest impact for multiple customers and internal security posture. KMS/HSM integration is medium effort but has a few long lead items (procurement, HSM vendor onboarding). Retention at 7 years is mostly policy + storage cost, but we need legal sign-off.

Alex: Legal prefers 7y retention as an opt-in enterprise feature. We should avoid defaulting to that for hosted customers. Need configurable retention per tenant and an export tool for audits.

Tony: SRE perspective — audit log throughput and storage tiering matter. For 1M events/day we can do hot storage 90d + cold storage for the rest, but retrieval SLA will be hours, not minutes. Is that acceptable?

Maya: Proposed prioritization: 1) SOC2 gap remediation (controls + infra) 2) Audit logs: baseline 1y hot + cold archive for up to 7y (opt-in enterprise) 3) KMS/HSM MVP for key wrapping + BYOK workflow (enterprise only). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Daniel: Agree. For roadmap/OKR wording we should have measurable launch criteria. Suggest: "SOC2 readiness: complete control mapping, automated evidence collection for 90% of controls, and run 1 internal audit by EoQ."

Sara: For audit logs, propose launch criteria: ```
- ingest pipeline verified at 1M events/day
- retention configurable per org (default 365d)
- export tool that can produce tamper-evident archive
- retrieval SLA documented (hot: <1h, cold: <24h)
```

Alex: Legal adds: retention config + deletion policy docs, customer-facing Data Processing Addendum updates, and playbook for eDiscovery.

Tony: For KMS/HSM MVP launch criteria: ```
- support for external HSM provider via standard API
- BYOK flow end-to-end (key import, usage, rotation)
- audit trail for key operations
- fallback to Redwood-managed keys if HSM unreachable
```

Maya: Resource ask — we need 2 engs for 6 weeks to close the SOC2 logging gaps, 1 infra eng for the audit log pipeline work, and 1 eng plus a security engineer for the KMS integration. Can product prioritize hires/time or defer HSM to after SOC2?

Daniel: We can frontload SOC2 to the first month of the quarter and then cycle infra to audit logs. HSM can be a second-half project unless a customer contract requires earlier delivery.

Sara: Dependencies: storage cost approval from finance, S3 lifecycle policy for cold archive, and retention UI flags from product. I'll draft infra PRD.

Alex: I'll draft the legal checklist and templates. Also double-check potential export encryption requirements for certain regulated customers.

Maya: Action items: @Sara draft infra PRD by Wed; @Alex legal checklist by Fri; @Daniel update OKRs with the measurable launch criteria; @Tony prepare test plan for ingest pipeline. I'll schedule a 30m sync Friday to finalize backlog order. :calendar: :thumbsup:

compliance-bot: Reminder — previous SOC2 epic (id: SOC2-42) has pending evidence items: access reviews (2), SIEM alert tuning (3). Please mark owners in the PRD.

Daniel: Noted. I'll own the OKR text and link PRD + legal checklist.

Maya: Great. If no objections I'll present this timeline in the exec review next Tuesday. :rocket:
